newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks post moderate gains at open.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks post moderate gains at open.

* Toronto stocks eased from opening highs to trade moderately stronger early on Tuesday. * Rising media and conglomerates were offset by continuing weakness in golds and energy.

Toronto stocks slipped from opening highs to trade moderately stronger early on Tuesday as rising communications, conglomerates and utilities were offset by further weakness in the gold and energy sectors.
Analysts said the market uptrend should hold, barring major interest rate or currency developments.

"They will continue on well into the summer, I think, unless something dramatic happens, like one of the G7 countries decided to increase interest rates precipitously or there's a currency problem," said Ira Katzin, an investment adviser at RBC Dominion Securities in Toronto.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index rose 6.18 points to 6473.59 in turnover of 13.5 million shares worth C$157.7 million.
Advancing stocks outpaced declines 258 to 227 while 241 issues were flat.
Ten of Toronto's 14 sub-indexes gained ground, led by communications, consumer products, conglomerates, metals and utilities.
Gold and oils continued to slip, while real estate and transportation traded nearly flat.

Katzin said investors would keep a close watch on economic indicators, especially in the U.S., to gauge economic growth ahead of the July 1 meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve's rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee.
"But as I said, there continues to be an awful lot of money sitting on the sidelines, waiting to find a home," he said.
--- HOT STOCKS ---

* Abacan Resource Corp shares rebounded slightly, gaining 0.50 to 3.57 in active early trade after losing 62 percent of their value yesterday. The Calgary-based oil firm said its cash flow in 1997 and 1998 would be much lower than analysts' forecasts.
* Ballard Power Systems Inc shares continued a strong two-week climb, rising 3.00 in early trade to 49.00.
